title.narrative: Catalysing the Green Transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina

description.narrative: “Catalysing the Green Transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina” is a 5-year programmatic framework, developed by UNDP in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in cooperation with governmental counterparts and international development partners. It leverages new development thinking and aims to catalyse and anchor a broader and just transformation towards a green and zero-carbon Bosnia and Herzegovina. Since the green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina has proven to be a complex development challenge, tackling a range of social, economic, and environmental systems, this programmatic framework is being developed based on a portfolio approach, in order to optimise impact and effectiveness. This framework recognises that individual, log-framed projects, presented as single-point “solutions”, are limited in terms of responding to system-level development priorities, ever-emerging challenges, and evolving contexts at scale. Instead, the portfolio is designed in a way that allows for faster adaptation to changing ecosystems and continuous learning around integrated solutions that cut across different sectors and address multiple dimensions of development simultaneously.The strategic intent of this framework is to contribute to accelerated decarbonisation and reduction of the CO2 footprint and green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the following change hypothesis: By empowering and inspiring people – policymakers, communities, businesses and entrepreneurs, scientists, innovators – and coming together to implement new integrated solutions and policies that enable switching from fossil fuels to clean energy production and consumption, reduce waste and pollution, minimize environmental crimes, introduce circular business models, protect and replenish natural resources or nurture sustainable lifestyles in society, UNDP and partners will catalyse a new momentum for a viable green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
